whatFailed: Step 2 called POST /v2/bookings/{uid}/mark-absent on the booking step 1 had just created for 2051-01-15T13:00:00Z and got 400 instead of 200, because cal.diy only allows a booking to be marked absent after its scheduled start time and the scenario never arranged for a booking that had started.

docClaim.quote: post /v2/bookings/{bookingUid}/mark-absent ... description: The provided authorization header refers to the owner of the booking. ... requestBody: required: true ... responses: '200': description: '' content: application/json: schema: $ref: '#/components/schemas/MarkAbsentBookingOutput_2024_08_13'. The page documents no other response and no precondition on the booking. The sibling help page in the same scanned corpus does state the precondition: "You can now mark guests as \"No Show\" for past bookings where one or more attendees did not attend." (.truecourse/specs/sources/cal.com-help/help/bookings/no-show.md:7)

observed: Step 1 created booking uid n96fHhyNNhAKqU8UUyrejq with start 2051-01-15T13:00:00.000Z (201, accepted). Step 2 posted {host: true, attendees: [{email, absent: true}]} with cal-api-version 2024-08-13 and got HTTP 400 in 27 ms: {"status":"error","error":{"code":"BadRequestException","message":"Bookings can only be marked as absent after their scheduled start time. Current time in UTC+0: 2026-08-13T10:50:37.824Z, Booking start time in UTC+0: 2051-01-15T13:00:00.000Z"}}. The request reached the real 2024-08-13 handler, so this is a semantic refusal, not a version or validation-shape problem. server.stderr.txt only shows the sandbox SMTP being absent (ECONNREFUSED ::1:1025 while sending the booking confirmation), which is unrelated.
impact: None for users: the refusal is correct, immediate and its message names the exact reason. The cost is coverage: because the scenario books 25 years into the future and marks absence one step later, the entire documented mark-absent contract (the 200 envelope, the 17 required booking-output fields, absentHost true and attendees[0].absent true) is never exercised, and steps 3 to 6 of the scenario never run.

rootCause.explanation: markAbsent loads the booking, computes nowUtc and the booking start in UTC, and throws BadRequestException when nowUtc < bookingStartTimeUtc, before calling handleMarkNoShow. This is a deliberate precondition, not a defect: it matches the product's own help documentation (no-show is an action on past bookings, reached from bookings/past) and the web UI, which only offers Mark as No Show on past bookings. Cited here as the code the scenario collided with, not as a bug. The scenario also had no documented way to reach the happy path: POST /v2/bookings refuses a start in the past (packages/lib/isOutOfBounds.tsx:10 BookingDateInPastError, mapped to 400 in apps/api/v2/src/platform/bookings/2024-08-13/services/errors.service.ts:47-48), so an eligible booking has to be seeded directly in the database.

notes:
Not an edition-mismatch and not the API-version systemic cause: step 2 sent cal-api-version 2024-08-13, which cal.diy does serve, and the request reached BookingsController_2024_08_13_markNoShow. Systemic cause 1 would have bitten step 3 (cal-api-version 2026-02-25, and the doc's operationId is BookingsController_2026_02_25_markNoShow while cal.diy tops out at 2024-08-13), but the run stopped at step 2.

Why test-defect rather than doc-bug: no API-reference page in this scanned corpus enumerates any 4xx for any bookings endpoint, so a page listing only a 200 is not a promise that every well-formed call succeeds; and a sibling page in the same corpus (cal.com-help/help/bookings/no-show.md) states plainly that no-show applies to past bookings. The scenario contradicted a doc it had already ingested and depended on state (a booking whose start time has passed) that it never set up.

Still worth filing as a documentation improvement, secondary to the verdict: the mark-absent endpoint description should state that the booking must have started and that the API answers 400 otherwise. The text is generated from the @ApiOperation description at apps/api/v2/src/platform/bookings/2024-08-13/controllers/bookings.controller.ts:395-401 in the tested tree, so the one-line fix lives in cal.diy as well as in whatever tree generates cal.com's published reference.

For the guard engine: this flow cannot pass as written. Either seed a booking with a past startTime directly (the create route refuses past starts) and mark absence against that, or drop the contract step and keep only the input-validation steps. Note that a seeded past booking would also let steps 4 to 6 (body required, empty attendees array, attendee entry missing absent) run against the real validator instead of dying behind the same 400.
